However, the Tennessee Supreme Court overturned his conviction, finding that the facts of the case did not warrant a first degree murder conviction. At his fourth trial, the prosecution chose to only try Westfield for manslaughter. On February 25, 1908, Westfield was acquitted and released from custody. It was determined that Constable Rains was abusive and had attacked Westfield, who had committed no crime, without any lawful justification. Constable Rains, who had been courting a local school teacher, became enraged by the noise being made from a nearby party at the home of Westfield's grandmother, where firecrackers and Roman candles were being set. Even as his own friends later tried to dissuade him, Rains attacked Westfield's grandmother's house, firing a shot through the door with his pistol. In response, Westfield shot and killed him. narrativeSummary: Joyce Lukezic and Robert Charles Cruz were both implicated as masterminds of the home-invasion murders of William "Pat" Redmond and his mother-in-law Helen Phelps on December 31, 1980. Redmond's wife and Phelps' daughter, Marilyn Redmond, survived the attack. Both Lukezic and Cruz were implicated in the contract killing by Arnold Merrill, who alleged that the crime was motivated by the desire to take over Redmond's printing business (Lukezic's husband Ron was business partners with Redmond at the time of the crime). In December 1981, Cruz was tried and convicted for first-degree murder, attempted murder, and conspiracy; he was sentenced to death in January 1982. Lukezic was tried and convicted of the same charges in August 1982. Following her conviction, a new trial was ordered for Lukezic, who was found guilty based on entirely circumstantial evidence. Prosecutors did not disclose that Merrill, a key prosecution witness, was provided with benefits and leniency for his testimony. After a second trial in April-May 1985 ended in a mistrial, Lukezic was acquitted of all charges at her third trial in November 1985. Cruz's death sentenced was overturned in October 1983, and two 1987 retrials ended in mistrials. In 1988, Cruz was convicted again at his fourth trial and re-sentenced to death; that conviction was overturned in 1993 on the basis that Hispanics had been excluded from his jury. In his fifth trial in 1995, Cruz argued that he was framed by Merrill who won immunity for his testimony. Cruz, like Lukezic, was acquitted of all charges.
